text:
Sophie (CS): Heads up — customer 'MapleApps' (EU region) opened a ticket: since ~09:00 UTC they see 250-400ms p95 latency and intermittent 401s. They ran a quick check and their requests appear to be resolving to our us-west Anycast IPs. Raising here to triage.

Maria (Support): Can you paste one example curl + response headers and the client-side resolver info from them? Also any user IPs or sample hostnames would help.

Sophie (CS): Paste from the customer:

curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
> < HTTP/2 401
> < x-region: us-west
> < x-request-id: rwd_abc123
> < date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:12:11 GMT

They also ran:
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com
52.32.10.11

And from their workstation (ISP resolver):
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com
52.32.10.11

So both resolver and response header indicate us-west. Customer is based in Amsterdam and expects eu-west routing.

Raj (Eng): Hmm. Two things to check: 1) why routing layer chose us-west (anycast mapping or fallback), 2) why 401 for some tokens when hitting us-west (token scoping mismatch?). Sophie can you confirm whether this customer is on Hosted or Dedicated? If Dedicated, token mapping could be region-scoped.

Sophie (CS): They are Hosted (standard). Token should be global. They only see 401 for ~10% of requests; most are 200 but high latency.

Maria (Support): Can the customer run a dig +trace and also query with edns-client-subnet to simulate their resolver? Example I asked them to run:

$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com +edns=0 +subnet=2.16.101.9
(we received) 34.95.8.77

Customer's ISP resolver: 52.32.10.11 (us-west) TTL=220

So looks like different upstream resolvers return different A records. Could be resolver-level caching at ISP or GeoIP mismatch in our authoritative DNS.

Ella (NetOps): I'm pulling authoritative DNS logs now. DNSMon: any recent changes to our geo records or healthcheck propagation?

DNSMon: Deploy activity: at 08:48 UTC we rotated a subset of eu-edge pool and briefly marked 34.95.8.77 (eu-west-edge-3) as draining for maintenance. Healthchecks show 34.95.8.77 failing for ~90s then recovered. No zone file changes.

Chris (SRE): That maintenance would cause health-based routing to avoid specific eu node IPs. However that should not cause global answers to resolve to us-west unless fallback/placement logic intentionally returns cross-region IPs for certain resolvers. What do our DNS logs show for the queries from the customer's resolver IP range?

Ella (NetOps): From query logs: resolver 77.88.33.12 (their ISP) received an answer pointing to 52.32.10.11 with TTL ~220 between 09:00:00 and 09:04:00. We also see the authoritative nameserver served eu IPs to other resolvers (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 returned eu). So looks like inconsistent answers depending on which caching resolver they use.

Raj (Eng): Two likely causes: (A) their ISP's resolver was already holding a cached us-west answer from earlier and is still within TTL, or (B) the ISP's resolver is peering into a PoP that maps to a us-west Anycast instance (resolver-level anycast/geo mismatch), or (C) a negative caching/EDNS client-subnet resolution mismatch where we don't get the client's subnet so we return default (us-west) for that resolver.

Maria (Support): Customer reports they restarted their home router and still see us-west. They cannot easily change resolver. Suggested temporary workaround: set system DNS to 1.1.1.1 or 9.9.9.9 — they tried 1.1.1.1 and requests resolved to eu IPs and latency improved.

Sophie (CS): The lingering issue is the 401s — could token validation be routed to a control plane in us-west that does not accept their token? Any evidence?

Raj (Eng): Check auth logs: pulling token validation logs for request id rwd_abc123 — shows authentication handled by us-west auth service and a small percentage (10%) failed with 401: token not found. This implies that either replication of session/token metadata between control plane regions is eventually consistent and during failover some keys may not be recognized immediately. We have an existing eventual consistency window for token propagation (~30s).

Chris (SRE): So combined story: customer DNS resolver returned us-west IP frequently (due to cache/anycast mismatch and a short maintenance window causing some eu nodes to drain). That caused some requests to go to us-west, where token metadata hadn't replicated yet, causing transient 401s. Fallback policy also may trigger cross-region routing aggressively when eu nodes report transient failures, amplifying the misrouting.

Ella (NetOps): Mitigations:
- Short term: Ask customer to switch to 1.1.1.1 (worked) or flush their resolver cache. Support checklist: ask for dig outputs from both their ISP resolver and a public resolver.
- Immediate platform fix: Reduce healthcheck drain jitter during maintenance windows and add brief sticky routing to prefer same-region answers for resolvers that recently received eu answers (cache affinity).
- DNS TTL: we currently use 300s for A records. Lowering TTL helps but increases load. Instead we can add low-ttl records for maintenance windows (we can programmatically flip TTL to 60s before planned drains).

Maria (Support): For this specific ticket I've asked the customer to use 1.1.1.1 and we confirmed improved latency and no 401s after switching. Customer is okay with that workaround but wants root cause. I've filed CS-8421 and marked P2.

Raj (Eng): Action items assigned:
- Raj/Ella: investigate resolver affinity heuristics and see why some resolvers get us-west by default. (ETA 24h)
- Chris: review fallback policy thresholds; reduce cross-region fallback aggressiveness for Hosted customers to avoid broad cross-region answers. (ETA 48h)
- Support: update KB article for "DNS caching and region routing" with steps for customers (include dig +edns guide, switching to public resolvers, how to check x-region header).

Chris (SRE): Quick defensive change we can roll in next patch: tag responses with an additional header x-routing-source: dns-cache=<resolver-ip> so we can more easily correlate trouble tickets to specific resolvers. I'd like to roll that in as non-breaking telemetry. DeployBot: can we schedule a small patch to add header and wire logs?

DeployBot: Deployment scheduled to canary at 23:00 UTC today (non-critical header-only change).

DNSMon: Note: we'll also add an alert if >2% of queries for a region are answered with remote-region IPs for more than 5 minutes — should help detect similar problems early.

Sophie (CS): Thanks all. I'll send a wrap-up to the customer: explanation, mitigation steps (switch DNS / flush / temporary TTL change during scheduled maintenance windows), and timeline for platform fixes. Closing loop in CS ticket CS-8421 once netops/eng confirm.

Maria (Support): One more note for runbook: advise customers with strict auth scoping to avoid cross-region fallback during sensitive operations; recommend using region pinning header for enterprise accounts if available.

Raj (Eng): I'll follow up with logs and a short write-up once I triage resolver logs. For now, root cause likely: transient eu pool drain + resolver caching/anycast mismatch -> cross-region routing -> token eventual-consistency gaps -> intermittent 401s.

Chris (SRE): Agreed. We'll also add a small post-incident blameless review for how maintenance interacts with DNS/healthchecks.
